_readme: WHO SOUNDS LIKE WHO. This file is the casting session and it is meant to be argued with.
One entry per NPC id, matching the ids in the module's npcs.js. Anything not listed uses the
voice  an edge-tts short name. `python tools/voice-generate.py --list-voices` prints every one
your machine can actually reach; the recorder checks yours against that list before it
cuts anything, so a typo is caught in a second rather than found at the table.
rate   speaking speed, e.g. -10% for someone who says as little as possible and means all of it.
pitch  in Hz, e.g. -8Hz. A little goes a long way. Past about 15Hz either way it stops sounding
like a person and starts sounding like a setting.
note   why. For you, in six months, when you wonder what you were going for.
The casting below is character-led, not name-led: a voice is picked for how the person in the
module behaves, and the accents are spread out mainly so that ten people in one corridor are
distinguishable with your eyes shut. Change any of it. Deleting a clip folder and re-running is
cheap, and hearing it is the only way to know.

sonya.note: Runs the base. Short sentences, no time for you, not panicking and resents anyone who makes that harder.

rosa.note: Blunt to the edge of rude, and doing two jobs. Quick and low: she has already decided.

dana.note: Stoic and sullen. Slow and flat on purpose — the pauses are the character.

rie.note: Everything is a bit until the last sentence. The lift is what makes the flat delivery of the useful line land.

morgan.note: Warm, chatty, and the chat is a coping strategy. Should sound like the nicest person here, because he is.

jerome.note: Jokes getting faster and worse for three weeks. Fast enough to be tiring, which is the point.

ashraf.note: Newest aboard, eager to be liked, agrees with whoever spoke last. Young and up.

kantaro.note: Withdrawn, sweating, stronger than last week. Low and slightly slow — something is using the throat.

giovanni.note: Pleasant, half a second late, never quite an answer. Slow and slightly bright is the whole trick: it is a person's voice at the wrong speed.
